newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: RUGBY LEAGUE-NZRL president apologises to Lions.
newsitem.headline: RUGBY LEAGUE-NZRL president apologises to Lions.

text.p: CHRISTCHURCH, Oct 29 - New Zealand Rugby League (NZRL) president Graham Carden has apologised for the absence of a liaison officer to assist the touring Great Britain team in Christchurch, NZPA reported on Tuesday.
The Lions arrived in Christchurch on Sunday to find a bus to take them to their hotel, but no one to greet them.
It prompted an outburst from British coach Phil Larder, who questioned whether his team were an embarrassment to the NZRL.
"We're a just a bit pissed off, we seem to have been pushed into a backwater," Larder said.
"We like the hotel but nobody from the NZRL has contacted us since we've been here."
Carden on Tuesday offered his apologies to the tourists and said the NZRL had moved quickly since Monday night to rectify the problem.
"The absence of a liaison officer is inexcusable. We appointed Don Wilson to the job and he decided at the last moment that he was unavailable," Carden said.
"I gather that he (Wilson) may have appointed someone of his own back to replace him, and whether this other person was given all the details and information, I don't know.
"Whatever it is, it is not good enough. We accept that we're disappointed that the person we appointed didn't take the matter seriously enough.
"I think apologies are in order and we do apologise to the British team for this oversight."
Carden said once he was informed of the situation, as were officials with the Kiwis squad, who are also based in Christchurch this week, moves were made to address the problem.
It is understood Kiwis coach Frank Endacott, who originally comes from Christchurch, acted to provide assistance for the British on Monday night.
